text: Perth is the letter still folded — its meaning is inside, and nothing you do from outside tells you what. It waits for the fold to give, not for you to guess. Gebo, the rune you carry, is the passing between two hands, nothing held back on either side. So they sit oddly together: you are the one who gives openly, and here is a thing that keeps itself until its own hour. What you hand over freely, this one holds.

Perth is what stays sealed while everything moves around it — the fold holds, and the shape inside is not shown by handling. Gebo is yours, the give and take that passes in the open between two. The two do not match easily: one is an exchange you can see, the other is something withheld until it decides. The letter is not refusing you. It is only not open yet.

Perth is the sealed letter — meaning held inside, not shown by handling. Gebo, which you carry, is the open passing between two hands. Set side by side they pull apart: one gives without keeping, the other keeps until it is ready. What that opens is the question of waiting — whether a thing withheld is a thing refused. The fold is still a fold.

Perth is what is folded shut, its inside unknown until the seal gives. Gebo is the giving that passes between two with nothing kept back — that is the rune you carry. Against each other they stand plainly: the open hand and the closed one. And what stands between them is time: the letter is not withholding from you, it is only not yet. Your hand is out. The fold has not turned.

Perth is the letter still folded. Whatever it says is already written; the fold is what stands between the writing and the reading. Handling it tells you nothing — the weight in the hand is the same whether the news is good or hard. It is a thing whose meaning is complete and not yet available.

Gebo is yours to carry: the passing between two hands with nothing kept on either side. It is not a trade, where each counts. It is the loaf broken and handed over, and the hand that takes it is as much part of the giving as the hand that offers.

Set the two together and they do not fit easily. You are the open hand; this is the closed one. What you do by nature — give it over, let it pass — is the one thing that will not work on a fold. The letter cannot be given into. It can only be waited out.

And that is what the tension opens: the difference between a thing withheld and a thing not yet ready. The sealed letter is not refusing you. Your hands go on moving around it, and the fold holds, and both of those are true at once.

Perth is the sealed thing. The fold lies flat and the letter stays where you set it, and nothing about the outside tells you what is written. Its meaning is not missing; it is enclosed. That is the whole of it — a shape whose inside waits.

Gebo is the rune you carry. It is what passes between two, hand to hand, with nothing held back on either side — the open exchange where neither party counts what is owed.

Those two do not sit comfortably. The open hand meets a thing that keeps. Everything you are good at — handing over, letting pass, meeting the other halfway — has no purchase on a fold. There is nothing here to give to, and nothing offered back.

What that opens is a question about waiting. The letter is not keeping something from you; it simply has not turned yet. Your hands move around it and the seal holds, and neither of those is the other's fault.
